description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of demonstrations and accuracy for different activation functions. The x-axis, labeled "#Demonstrations", has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1500, with tick labels at intervals of 250. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy", also has a linear scale, ranging from 45 to 55, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The plot contains four lines, each representing a different activation function: Squared-Exponential (dark blue, solid line, circle markers), Tanh (blue, solid line, circle markers), ELU (light blue, solid line, circle markers), and LLaMA-2-chat-7B (pink, dashed line). The Squared-Exponential line starts at around 52 at 0 demonstrations and increases to approximately 57 at 250 demonstrations, remaining steady at 57 until 1500 demonstrations. The Tanh line begins at around 47 at 0 demonstrations, increases to approximately 48 at 250 demonstrations, and remains steady at 48 until 1500 demonstrations. The ELU line starts at around 47 at 0 demonstrations and increases to approximately 48 at 250 demonstrations, remaining steady at 48 until 1500 demonstrations. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B line remains constant at around 43 across the entire range of demonstrations.
